 Learn more CVB Financial has delivered strong share returns over the past few years, which naturally raises the question of whether those gains line up with the returns the bank earns on its capital. With the stock recently closing at US$22.58, the key issue for investors is how firmly that price rests on the profitability of the capital the business deploys. 
 Over the last 3 years the share price has advanced 45.0%. That places more focus on whether the underlying returns on capital can support that kind of wealth creation. 
 The banking group relies on how efficiently it can turn deposits and other funding into interest income and fee revenue, so its ability to keep earning solid returns on loans and securities may support or limit what investors are prepared to pay for each dollar of equity. 
 If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why CVB Financial's 17.2x P/E tells a different valuation story . 
 The issue now is whether the returns CVB Financial earns on its capital are strong and consistent enough to justify where the stock trades today. 
 If you want to test the same question about the returns companies earn on their capital across a broader set of ideas, start with 29 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Is CVB Financial Still Cheap on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model looks at how much profit CVB Financial can earn over and above the return shareholders require. On this view, the bank starts from a Book Value of $17.84 per share and an Average Return on Equity of 10.14%, which feeds into a Stable EPS estimate of $1.96 per share based on inputs from 5 analysts. Against a Cost of Equity of $1.40 per share, that leaves an Excess Return of $0.56 per share, so the framework assumes CVB Financial can keep generating earnings that exceed the charge for using shareholder capital. 
 Those cash profits are paired with a Stable Book Value projection of $19.37 per share, again sourced from analyst estimates, which implies the equity base itself continues to grow rather than shrink. Put next to a market price of US$22.58, the Excess Returns projections place CVB Financial's estimated intrinsic value substantially above the current share price. They explain which paths for future growth, profitability and earnings would need to occur for the shares to appear meaningfully cheaper or more expensive than today's quote.
